conventions.convention: Reverse edges carry inverse group elements. Holonomy multiplies links in traversal order, with the first traversed edge on the left. Vertex transformations are U_e ↦ h_s(e) U_e h_t(e)^{-1}.

Finite powers carry product smooth structures and product Borel measures; the empty link space is a singleton with unit point mass, and empty sums are zero. The bi-invariant probability is supplied as data, rather than obtained by invoking Haar existence under countable choice.
The Gauss sector consists of L² equivalence classes fixed by every vertex transformation. Infinitesimal Gauss equations alone are not asserted to impose invariance under disconnected components.
Wilson loops use a smooth unitary representation of positive dimension d and normalized trace Tr/d. Empty loops have identity holonomy; reversal complex-conjugates the normalized trace.

SU(2) uses its defining two-dimensional representation, τ(U)=Tr(U)/2=x₀, and the pushforward of normalized round S³ area. The Wilson action is βΣ_p(1−τ(U_p)); β=4/g₀² when a positive bare coupling is used.

Plaquette factorization uses a finite planar rectangle with free boundary and no periodic identifications. All horizontal links and the vertical links in a chosen column are fixed to identity by a root-fixed gauge transformation. The independent variables are the resulting P_i,j=V_i+1,j V_i,j^{-1}. General compact topological groups must additionally supply product measurability of multiplication.

The area-law theorem restricts to 0<β≤1 and nondegenerate axis-aligned rectangles. Area counts enclosed plaquettes; σ_lat=−log λ is dimensionless. The conclusion asserts no continuum, infinite-volume, mass-gap, or continuum-confinement result.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC_ω, finite oriented lattice data specify a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group, link configurations, inverse reverse links, traversal-ordered face holonomies, the endpoint vertex action, a supplied normalized bi-invariant probability, continuous conjugation- and inversion-invariant face potentials, normalized finite-lattice expectations, the group-invariant L² Gauss sector, and infinitesimal directional derivatives.

Assume AC_ω, a compact topological group with product-measurable multiplication and normalized bi-invariant Borel probability, a finite positive-size planar rectangle with free boundary, and positive continuous conjugation- and inversion-invariant face weights. In the stated root-fixed tree gauge, P_i,j=V_i+1,j V_i,j^{-1} are independent, with probability w_i,j(g)dμ(g)/∫w_i,j dμ.

Assume AC_ω and β>0 with the specified SU(2) round measure and Wilson weight. The measure is a normalized bi-invariant Borel probability; I₀>0, 0<λ=I₁/I₀<1, and ∫U dν_β(U)=λ(β)I₂. As β↓0, λ(β)=β/4+O(β³).

Under the stated finite-graph, unitary-representation and AC_ω hypotheses, U_C(k·U)=k_v₀ U_C(U)k_v₀^{-1}. The normalized trace is gauge invariant and unchanged by cyclic rebasing; reversal gives its complex conjugate, including the empty-word case.

Under AC_ω and the stated finite lattice, compact Lie-group, supplied bi-invariant probability and continuous class-action hypotheses, the vertex formulas define a smooth action, face holonomies transform by conjugation, link measure and Boltzmann weight are invariant, and 0<Z_Λ<∞. The invariant L² subspace is closed, and the stated infinitesimal generators are defined on smooth functions.

Assume AC_ω and the specified finite free-boundary SU(2) Wilson lattice with 0<β≤1. For every contained axis-aligned rectangle of area A=(b−a)(d−c), ⟨W(C_a,b;c,d)⟩_β=λ(β)^A=exp(−σ_lat(β)A), with 0<λ<1 and σ_lat=−log λ>0. The center is {I₂,−I₂}, with nontrivial defining central character. No infinite-volume or continuum conclusion follows.

concerns.concern: The opening paragraph says, “No connection, principal bundle sector, action functional, or continuum theory is part of the lattice data below.” Later the same Definition chooses face potentials and explicitly defines “the dimensionless lattice action” S_Λ(U)=Σ_p Φ_p(U_p). The exclusion of an action functional contradicts the finite action actually included. Clarify whether the intended exclusion concerns a continuum action functional.

seams_checked.note: Checked the page inventories, def-qftx-nonabelian-gauge-data and its lattice consumers. The consumers retain the compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group, T_eG Lie algebra, smooth unitary representation and AC_ω assumptions. They do not invoke bundle sectors or connections. The generalized factorization lemma explicitly supplies joint measurability for general compact groups and separately verifies the Lie-group specialization.

Checked the regulator page, its SU(2) group and transfer well-definedness lemmas, and its postulate against the finite lattice-data Definition. They preserve the endpoint action, inverse reverse links, ordered face words, supplied bi-invariant probability and invariant face potentials. Full AC explicitly supplies AC_ω. The periodic four-dimensional regulator does not invoke the free-boundary two-dimensional factorization or area-law theorem; its slice Gauss sector and transfer operator are separately defined and justified.
